article.title: Americans have never had more of their money in stocks — not even in the dot-com bubble: Chart of the Day

article.title: Solar-powered 'leaf' generates hydrogen while purifying seawater
article.summary:
Inspired by leaves, which harness solar power to generate oxygen and carry out other processes, researchers at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore have developed a solar-powered device that generates hydrogen from seawater while simultaneously degrading hydrazine, a highly toxic industrial wastewater pollutant.
In conventional water electrolysis, hydrogen is produced at the cathode (negative electrode), while oxygen is released at the anode (positive electrode).
At the cathode, water molecules gain electrons and produce hydrogen gas, while at the anode, they lose electrons to produce oxygen.
As an alternative, the researchers developed an anode that, instead of producing oxygen, breaks down hydrazine, a highly toxic industrial pollutant.
